architecture.mechanism: Hot coolant degrades sealing/insulating performance — as coolant temperature and conductivity rise, insulation resistance drops and permeable micro-paths open through materials that remain sealed when cold, so leaks appear only at operating temperature under driving conditions.
architecture.intervention: Add UV fluorescent dye to the coolant, road-test the vehicle until full operating temperature is reached (not static idle), then inspect the driver-side heater core, its hoses/connections, and the coolant reservoir cap with a UV lamp; supplement with a hot-system pressure test at operating temperature.
architecture.expected_effect: A leak path invisible during cold static idling will reveal dye traces or pressure drop at operating temperature, localizing the vapor source (most likely the driver-side heater core or a hot-only weep path).
architecture.falsification_test: If a full-temperature road test with dye plus a hot pressure test yields no dye traces and no pressure drop, the coolant-leak hypothesis is falsified (smell likely from normal vapor venting or an external source); a measured spike in coolant conductivity after driving would support coolant degradation as a contributing path.

challenge.kill_reason: all deterministic checks passed; the adversarial gauntlet's objections are ESCALATED (uncalibrated attacker, Art. L) and ride the record for adjudication
